title: Exhaled nitric oxide test (FeNO)
what: You breathe out slowly into a small device. It shows whether there is a certain type of inflammation in your airways.
why: When asthma is suspected, and to check how well inhaler treatment is working.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: Which inhalers and medicines you use
If you recently had a cold

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually do not eat or drink anything except water for 1 hour before. You are often asked to avoid nitrate-rich foods before the test, like beets and leafy salad. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Do not smoke on the day of the test.

prepare.title: Exercise
prepare.text: No exercise for an hour before the test.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your inhalers on your own. Tell your doctor when you last used them.

bring: A list of your medicines and inhalers
steps: You take a deep breath in through the mouthpiece
You breathe out slowly and evenly for about 10 seconds
A guide on the screen helps you keep the right force
It is usually repeated 2 to 3 times
feel: Sometimes it is hard to breathe out evenly. The screen guide helps
after: The result is usually shown right away
Your doctor will explain it along with other tests
You can go back to your usual day right away

faq.a: It shows inflammation in the airways. Your doctor makes the diagnosis together with other tests.
Yes, usually from age 5 or 6, if the child can breathe out evenly.

reminders.text: FeNO test tomorrow. Do not smoke in the morning. Do not eat or exercise for an hour before the test.
